les: Galileo kyk self na die hemel

items.bewering: Galileo was 'n Italiaanse wiskundige en sterrekundige.
items.bron: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com/print/article/224058): Italian natural philosopher, astronomer and mathematician, born Pisa; EBSCO Research Starters 'Galileo' (Italian astronomer and mathematician).

items.bewering: Hy het later as Leonardo da Vinci gelewe en is eers ná Leonardo se dood gebore.
items.bron: Leonardo died 2 May 1519 at Amboise (Château d'Amboise biography, chateau-amboise.com; Royal Collection Trust, rct.uk). Galileo born 15 February 1564 (Britannica; INCOIS lecture notes). Galileo was born 45 years after Leonardo's death.

items.bewering: Hy het ook ná die seereise van Dias en Da Gama gelewe.
items.bron: Dias rounded the Cape in 1488 and Da Gama sailed to India in 1497-1499 (Museo Galileo, 'The circumnavigation of Africa', mostre.museogalileo.it; University of Pretoria Historia journal). Galileo lived from 1564 to 1642, so the sequence holds.

items.bewering: Sy werk staan aan die begin van wat ons vandag wetenskap noem.
items.bron: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Galileo Galilei' (plato.stanford.edu/entries/galileo): since the 17th century many have seen Galileo as the 'father' of modern science, and 'Galilean science' is used as a synonym for modern scientific method. The wording 'staan aan die begin van' (stands at the start of) rather than 'het uitgevind' (invented) is properly hedged, and science before him is not denied.

items.bewering: In die Nederlande het iemand 'n nuwe kykglas gemaak wat ver dinge nader laat lyk.
items.bron: Hans Lipperhey of Middelburg showed his spyglass in The Hague in September/October 1608 and was refused a patent; the instrument became known as the 'Dutch spyglass', magnifying about 3x (Springer, Experimental Astronomy 10.1007/s10686-009-9160-y; Museo Galileo, brunelleschi.imss.fi.it). The unnamed 'iemand' (someone) avoids the disputed question of who was first, which is correct.

items.bewering: Galileo het daarvan gehoor en sy eie een gebou.
items.bron: Springer, Experimental Astronomy 10.1007/s10686-009-9160-y and Museo Galileo: in 1609 Galileo learned of the Dutch device from reports and built his own. Sources differ on whether he had also seen a copy in Venice; the lesson's 'gehoor' (heard of it) holds either way.

items.bewering: Hy het dit keer op keer verbeter en skerper gemaak.
items.bron: Magnification went from about 3x to 8x (August 1609) and then to about 20x or close to 30x by late 1609 (Springer 10.1007/s10686-009-9160-y; mivision.com.au 'The telescope 400 years on'). He ground his own lenses with a stronger curve (University of Oklahoma Libraries, galileo.ou.edu), and Greco et al. (arXiv 1307.4963) show that he worked on resolution and illumination as well as magnification. Note: 'skerper' (sharper) is supported as 'shows finer detail'; no source ranks his image sharpness against other instruments.

items.bewering: Toe draai hy dit op na die hemel.
items.bron: He improved the instrument through 1609 and observed the Moon at the end of 1609 and Jupiter from 7 January 1610 (astronomy.com 'Jan. 7, 1610'; NASA '415 years ago'). The sequence holds. The lesson does not claim he was the first to point a telescope at the sky (Thomas Harriot drew the Moon earlier, in July 1609), and that is correct.

items.bewering: Hy het die teleskoop dus nie self uitgevind nie.
items.bron: Van Helden's 1977 monograph corrected the old error that Galileo invented the telescope (Historical Astronomy Division, AAS, had.aas.org/node/27); the Dutch spyglass of 1608 came before him.

items.bewering: Geleerdes van sy tyd het geglo die dinge in die hemel is glad en volmaak.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: Huntington Library, 'Sidereus Nuncius' (huntington.org): the discoveries directly challenged Aristotle's view that the heavens are perfect and unchanging; History of Science Museum Oxford, 'Mountains on the moon' (cabinet.ox.ac.uk): a perfect sphere would have shown a smooth terminator.

items.bewering: Deur sy teleskoop het hy berge en skaduwees op die maan gesien.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: History of Science Museum Oxford, 'Mountains on the moon' (Van Helden's 1989 translation of Sidereus Nuncius): an uneven terminator, and bright peaks in the dark part like mountaintops at dawn; Kent State special collections: dark patches explained as shadows of mountains and low regions.

items.bewering: Die maan is dus nie 'n gladde bal nie.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: Huntington Library: he concluded that the Moon is not a perfectly smooth sphere but has mountains and valleys.

items.bewering: By Jupiter het hy vier mane gesien wat om die planeet draai.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: NASA, '415 Years Ago: Astronomer Galileo Discovers Jupiter's Moons' (nasa.gov); National Geographic Education, 'Galileo Discovers Jupiter's Moons'; astronomy.com: first seen 7 January 1610, four moons by 13 January, and he concluded by 15 January that they orbit Jupiter.

items.bewering: Venus het ook fases net soos ons eie maan.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Phases of Venus' with its references, and History of Science Museum Oxford, 'The phases of Venus, 1610-23' (cabinet.ox.ac.uk): Venus goes through a complete set of phases much like the Moon, from thin crescent to full disc. Mapping checked: the comparison carries only the shape sequence, and the cause is also the same (sunlight on a sphere seen from changing angles), so a learner who reasons further is not misled. The one way the comparison falls short is that Venus also changes greatly in apparent size; the sentence does not touch on size, so it does not mislead.

items.bewering: Soms lyk dit vol en rond en soms net soos 'n dun stukkie lig.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Phases of Venus' and NASA APOD 'Phases of Venus' (science.nasa.gov): Venus goes from thin crescent to (nearly) full disc and back.

items.bewering: Byna almal in Galileo se tyd het geglo dat alles om die Aarde draai.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Ptolemaic system' and 'geocentric system': the Earth-centred model, with a stationary Earth, persisted until the Copernican system and Kepler's laws displaced it in the 16th and 17th centuries. Vatican Observatory, 'Heliocentrism condemned 400 years ago' (vaticanobservatory.org): the 1616 decree declared the Earth's motion false. The quantifier 'byna almal' (nearly everyone) correctly leaves room for the few Copernicans (Kepler, Digges).

items.bewering: Die vier mane wat hy by Jupiter gesien het, was van sy sterkste getuienis daarteen.
items.bron: astronomy.com 'Jan. 7, 1610' and National Geographic Education: the moons gave strong evidence that not everything revolves around the Earth. 'Van sy sterkste' (among his strongest) is a hedged superlative, and it is aimed at the right target, the claim that EVERYTHING orbits the Earth, which Jupiter's moons refute directly. Context: Oxford calls the phases of Venus his most decisive evidence against Ptolemy, which is why the lesson's 'among' rather than 'the strongest' is the correct form.

items.bewering: Hier was dinge wat jy self kon sien draai om iets anders as die Aarde.
items.bron: astronomy.com and Tel Aviv University 'The moons of Jupiter' (tau.ac.il): night after night the moons changed position but stayed with Jupiter; anyone with a telescope could repeat the observation.

items.bewering: Galileo het ook gesê dat die Aarde self om die Son beweeg.
items.bron: His 1632 Dialogue on the Two Chief World Systems defends the heliocentric system, and his trial was about teaching Copernicanism (Renaissance Quarterly review, Cambridge Core; Bridwell Library exhibit 'Galileo, Dialogo').

items.bewering: Daardie idee was nie sy eie nie, want die geleerde Kopernikus het dit voor hom voorgestel.
items.bron: Vatican Observatory: Copernicus's De revolutionibus was published in 1543, the year he died, 21 years before Galileo was born. The lesson does not claim that Copernicus was the very first to propose it (Aristarchus came earlier), so no superlative risk.

items.bewering: Galileo se waarnemings deur die teleskoop het daardie ou idee ondersteun.
items.bron: NASA and National Geographic: the Jupiter moons supported the Copernican theory; Oxford 'The phases of Venus': the observations fit the Copernican system but did not prove it uniquely (the Tychonic system also accommodated them). 'Ondersteun' (supported), rather than 'bewys' (proved), is exactly the right strength.

items.bewering: Die kerkleiers van sy tyd het die idee verwerp, en party geleerdes ook.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Vatican Observatory, 'Heliocentrism condemned 400 years ago on March 5': the decree of the Congregation of the Index of 5 March 1616 declared the Earth's motion false and contrary to Scripture. Opposition from Aristotelian scholars is supported by the same sources and by Britannica's account of geocentrism as the prevailing view.

items.bewering: Hy is verhoor en hy moes sê dat hy die idee terugtrek.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Museo Galileo, '08 Processo' (brunelleschi.imss.fi.it): summoned by the Inquisition in 1633; the trial ended on 22 June 1633 and he was forced to abjure.

items.bewering: Hy moes sy laaste jare in sy eie huis bly.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Museo Galileo '08 Processo': on 1 December 1633 he was allowed to return to Arcetri, which the page calls 'his home', where he lived under restrictions until his death in 1642; Wikipedia 'Villa Il Gioiello': lifelong house arrest at Il Gioiello from early 1634. Detail for the record: Il Gioiello was a villa he had RENTED since 1631, and after the trial he first spent a few months in Rome and Siena. 'In sy eie huis' is true in the sense of 'at home rather than in a prison', which is how a learner will read it; it is not a statement about ownership.

items.bewering: Hy is nie gemartel nie en ook nie in 'n tronk gesit nie.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Maurice Finocchiaro, 'Prison and Torture as False but Well-Founded Myths' (UNLV Digital Scholarship, philosophy_fac_articles/118): he was interrogated under a verbal threat of torture but not tortured, and was never held in an actual prison. Museo Galileo itinerary 'The Trial': during the hearings he stayed in the fiscal's apartments in the Holy Office, not in a cell. Universidad de Navarra, 'Lo que deberíamos saber sobre Galileo': never tortured. Nuance for the record: a sentence of imprisonment WAS pronounced on paper and commuted to house arrest the next day. The lesson's 'nie in 'n tronk gesit nie' (not put in a prison) describes what physically happened, and is correct.

items.bewering: Galileo het verander hoe 'n mens weet of 'n antwoord reg is. 'n Antwoord moet klop met wat jy self kan sien en meet, ook wanneer almal iets anders glo.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy 'Galileo Galilei': 'Galilean science' as a synonym for modern scientific method; EBSCO Research Starters: Galileo helped establish the modern scientific method through observation and experiment; New World Encyclopedia 'Galileo Galilei': pioneering quantitative experiments analysed mathematically. 'Sien en meet' (see and measure) maps onto observation and measurement. The sentence does not say he did it alone, so the attribution is acceptable.

items.bewering: teleskoop: 'n Buis met glase wat ver dinge nader en groter laat lyk.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia 'Telescope' and Dictionary.com 'telescope': an optical instrument that makes distant objects look larger, a tube with an objective lens (refractor) or a concave mirror (reflector). Read alone, the entry describes a refractor such as Galileo's; reflectors use (glass) mirrors, which 'glase' still covers loosely. A simplification that does not cross into falsehood at Grade 6.

items.bewering: sterrekundige: Iemand wat die sterre en die planete bestudeer en meet.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com 'astronomer': a scientist who studies objects in the sky such as stars and planets, and observes and measures them. The entry names stars and planets as examples without excluding other bodies; not false.

items.bewering: fase: Die vorm waarin jy die maan of Venus op 'n keer sien.
items.bron: astro4edu.org glossary (IAU Office of Astronomy for Education) 'phase': the shape of the sunlit part of a body as seen by an observer at a particular time, best known for the Moon, and Venus shows the same. The entry does not claim that ONLY the Moon and Venus have phases (Mercury has them too), so no false restriction.

items.bewering: verhoor: Die saak in 'n hof waar albei kante gehoor word.
items.bron: University of the Free State / PanSALB terminology database (pokello.ufs.ac.za, item 30377): 'verhoor' = trial, a judicial examination of matters of fact or law to determine the rights of the parties; Spil Plus (spilplus.journals.ac.za): 'billike verhoor' (fair trial) in the court sense. Mapping onto Galileo checked: the Inquisition was a church court before which he was interrogated and submitted a written defence (Museo Galileo), so the entry does not lead a learner astray about his trial.

opsomming: All 30 checkable claims are confirmed, including both superlatives ('aan die begin van', 'van sy sterkste', each correctly hedged) and the Venus-Moon comparison. Two places are worth a person's attention, though neither is wrong: Galileo's home at Arcetri was a rented villa ('in sy eie huis' holds as 'at home, not in prison'), and a prison sentence was pronounced on paper and commuted the next day, so 'nie in 'n tronk gesit nie' is right because he was never physically jailed (Finocchiaro).
